summary: The builder (bool-build-rows-r6.mjs) passes, all 936 cited case files exist, and 12 stored cases replay identically; new guards G3, G19, G20, G21 held against my variants of thin-overlap radii up to r1000, lenses and thin caps. But G7 (tangent pinch) only reads box and cylinder primitives, so the same two-side and four-side tangent cut built through a round pull() tool, a pull() plate or a joined plate is a silent wrong solid on the guarded path.

defects.feature: row 67/68 'cylinder through a box tangent to TWO or THREE sides' (guard G7, booleans.guard.mjs lines 379-397)
defects.problem: G7 does `if (!isPlainBox(a.d) || !b.d.prim || ...) continue`, so it only fires when the target is a box() primitive and the tool a cylinder() primitive. A tool made by pull() of a sketch circle, a plate made by pull() of a square sketch, or a plate made by join() of two boxes skips it. Guarded results: cr-pull-tool-tan2 built with 1 body/2 shells/9 faces (OCCT 2 solids/12 faces); cr-pull-tool-tan4 built vol 6869.80 vs closed form 6867.26 (3.7e-4, over the 3e-4 bar) with 1 body vs 4 solids; cr-pull-plate-tan2 and cr-joined-plate-tan2 same as tan2. Tan1 control passes correctly. These are exactly the pinch class the row says is refused, built as a silent wrong solid. Row 107 itself says the sibling G3 rule covers 'however it was made (round pull)', so the omission is not documented for G7.

Over-refuses an ordinary thin-wall tube: cylinder d100 h20 minus coaxial cylinder d99 (wall 0.5, remainder 1.99 percent) is refused as 'very thin sliver'; raw kernel result is correct (cr-o-tube2: dVol 2.1e-5, faces 4/4, 1 solid). Wall 1 mm (3.96 percent) builds. The 3 percent figure is justified only by cone/ball data; thin caps and segments I tried (ball r100 h21/22/25/40, r300 h64, cylinder segment r50-r300 3.07 percent) all stayed inside the bar at 1.7e-4 to 2.6e-4, so the rule is safe but its margin on segments is thin (2.6e-4 of 3e-4).

defects.feature: G19 (row 113) false refusal for large curved operands
defects.problem: G19 uses the kernel's tessellated bounding box of a CURVED operand as the 'independent' box. cylinder r800 has x min 21.0124 (true 21), so keep(box 100x1000x20, cylinder r800 dipping 29 mm) is refused with 'came out bigger than the shapes' although the unguarded result is correct (cr-keep-cyl-r800-d29: dVol 2.5e-4, dBbox 1.5e-13). The sentence is untrue for this case. The check is only exact for axis-aligned box operands. (r6h-top-keep-r300-d12 is a true positive: raw bbox z min -1.9983 vs -2, 8.4e-4.)
Over-refuses a thin plate clipped by a ball: keep(box 260x260x3, sphere d200) is refused ('overlap less than 10 mm'); raw result is correct (cr-o-plate-ball-keep dVol 4.8e-5).
Two parallel cylinders both turned to a generic angle are called 'cross at an angle' (any oblique axis), so keep of a parallel lens at [30,20,10] gets the wrong sentence (G2 not G20).
Group roll-up is still 'wrong' through row 124 (fz23-087-sph-box-uni built something different from OCCT). Honestly labelled, but the group still contains one acknowledged unguarded wrong solid.
